description: The figure is a multi-level (sunburst-style) pie chart representing medical ethics principles and their associated subtopics, showing 4 main inner slices and a larger set of outer slices that subdivide each principle; the inner ring contains four categories: Beneficence (dark blue, roughly about half of the circle), Autonomy (green, roughly about a quarter), Non-Maleficence (purple, roughly about a sixth), and Justice (orange/red, roughly about a tenth). The outer ring shows 26 labeled sub-slices in total, each in a lighter tint matching its parent principle: under Beneficence (light blues; 12 slices) are “Recognize the Responsibility of the Occupation,” “Comply with Laws and Regulations,” “Provide Medical Care to Patients,” “Continual Learning,” “Provide Assistance in Emergency,” “Respect and Cooperate with Colleagues,” “Respect Life, Dignity of Patients,” “Give Top Priority to Patients’ Interest in Conflict of Interest,” “Minimizing Conflicts of Interest,” “Ethical Research,” “Open Discussion and Fair Charging of Fees,” and one additional small blue slice at the boundary that is difficult to read; under Autonomy (light greens; 8 slices) are “Physician Can Freely Choose Whom to Serve,” “Make Responsible and Independent Clinical Judgement,” “Professional Relationship with Patients and Their Relatives,” “Keep Confidential of Patients’ Information,” “Maintain Truthful, Factual Communication,” “Respect Patients’ Rights to be Informed,” “Informed Freedom of Choice,” and “Human Decision-making of Incompetent/Competent Patient” (text partially small but legible in parts); under Non-Maleficence (light purples; 4 slices) are “Prevent Patient from Harm,” “Maintain Qualified Men Providing Medical Care,” “Report Unethical and Unprofessional Conduct,” and “Do Not Use Medicine for Personal Gain”; under Justice (light oranges; 2 slices) are “Promote Environmental Sustainability” and “Allocate Medical Sources Fairly,” with additional small justice-related labels visible near the top such as “Promote the Health of Community and Public Education” and “Treat Patients Fairly and Equally” appearing as narrow orange segments. The chart uses direct text labels on slices (no separate legend), shows no numeric percentage annotations, and no slices appear exploded or otherwise emphasized; visually, the largest inner slice is Beneficence, followed by Autonomy, then Non-Maleficence, then Justice.
